goal: Cross-check the existing interview catalog against Ukrainian and international interview-question banks, deduplicate by concept and interview intent, strengthen source evidence, and add only genuinely missing concepts.

rules: Do not create a new catalog question for wording-only variants.
Theory and scenario questions may remain separate when they test different interview intent.
A source hit strengthens source evidence and prevalence; it does not automatically create another question.
Absence from the current catalog is necessary but not sufficient for adding a question: recurrence and interview value must also justify it.
Official documentation validates answer correctness but is not by itself an interview-prevalence signal.
Ukrainian and international interview banks have equal priority as prevalence evidence.
Broad question banks, interviewer-authored guidance, hiring-derived sources and fresh market snapshots are tracked separately.

batches.label: DOU 250+ and DOU 400+

sources.title: DOU — 400+ QA interview questions for Junior, Middle, Senior

confirmedFindings: DOU 400+ contains internal wording/concept duplicates; 416 is a raw count, not a unique-question count.
Large parts overlap with DOU 250+, especially Selenium, Web/API, Mobile and practical scenarios.
DOU 400+ remains a first-class Ukrainian-market signal; overlap should strengthen evidence rather than make the source disposable.

Its practical tail is more valuable than much of its trivia: release pressure, incomplete testing, ambiguity, developer disagreement, debugging and late QA involvement require intent-level comparison.
The author says some questions came from interviews and most were collected while studying testing material; the list is useful coverage evidence but not proof that every item is frequent.
observedInternalDuplicateExamples: Database-type and relational-database concepts recur across sections.
Emulator vs simulator is split into overlapping questions.
Testing without documentation appears in overlapping forms.
